shared_elements: low relief carving of a procession scene
horizontal band of repeated rosettes/floral discs at the base
human figures in profile with detailed patterned headgear/hair (partly visible in A)
large disc/circular form (wheel in A, rosettes in B)
justification: Both surfaces show a low-relief processional frieze on a single register bounded below by a continuous band of repeated rosette discs, with profile human figures whose hair/beards are rendered as dense stippled or beaded texture, and profile animals (a chariot horse team in A, rams in B) whose bodies carry patterned incised infill — a very specific shared set of conventions. The main difference in content is the subject focus: A centres on a many-spoked chariot wheel and vehicle, while B shows led rams and a queue of standing tribute-bearers with vessels, and no wheeled vehicle.
